mainTopic: Rain in its season, the stories of חוני המעגל, and the start of the story of his grandson אבא חלקיה
overview: The עמוד opens by finishing a ברייתא about rain 'in its season' (בעתם): rain that falls on Tuesday and Friday nights, when no one is outside. Two stories support it. In the days of שמעון בן שטח the crops grew huge, and in the days of הורדוס rain fell only at night while the בית המקדש was being built. The גמרא then tells the famous story of חוני המעגל. He drew a circle, swore not to leave it until it rained, and fine-tuned his prayer until the right rain came. Because he would not pray for good to be removed, he brought a פר הודאה and asked for the rain to stop. שמעון בן שטח says he would have put חוני in נידוי, but he cannot, since ה׳ treats חוני like a beloved son. The סנהדרין praise him with a פסוק from איוב. A second story tells how חוני slept for seventy years, woke to find no one who believed him, and died, which leads to רבא's saying 'או חברותא או מיתותא'. The עמוד ends by starting the story of his grandson אבא חלקיה, whom two scholars find hoeing in a field; the story continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: What 'in their season' means
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains that rain 'in its season' (בעתם) means rain that falls on Tuesday nights and Friday nights.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'In their season' means on Wednesday eves (Tuesday nights) and on שבת eves (Friday nights).
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains the word בעתם from the blessing of rain in the פסוק. It says the ideal rain falls on specific nights.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On these two nights people normally stayed indoors. On Tuesday nights they feared harmful spirits, and on Friday nights it was שבת. Rain at these times waters the fields without getting in anyone's way. So the blessing is about timing, not only about how much rain falls.

keyTerms.meaning: In their season, meaning at the right time

steps.confusionAlert: 'לילי רביעיות' does not mean Wednesday night. The Jewish day starts at night, so the 'night of Wednesday' is what we call Tuesday night. In the same way, 'לילי שבתות' is Friday night.

phrases.english: 'In their season' —
phrases.notes: Quoting the word from the פסוק of blessing (ויקרא כו:ד)

phrases.english: means on Wednesday eves (Tuesday nights)
and on Shabbat eves (Friday nights).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from the previous daf about rain as a blessing
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rain 'in its season' means rain on Tuesday and Friday nights, when it disturbs no one.

steps.title: The days of שמעון בן שטח as an example
steps.stepSummary: In the days of שמעון בן שטח, rain fell only on those two nights, and the crops grew to an amazing size. Samples were saved to teach later generations how much sin costs us.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we found in the days of שמעון בן שטח: rain fell for them on Tuesday nights and Friday nights. The wheat grew as big as kidneys, the barley as big as olive pits, and the lentils as big as gold coins. They tied up samples of these crops for future generations, to show how much damage sin causes. As the פסוק says: 'Your iniquities have turned away these things, and your sins have withheld the good from you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings a real historical example to show what 'rain in its season' looks like. It shows how much blessing it brought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This story supports the meaning given in Step 1. When the people were worthy, rain came at exactly those times and the crops were enormous. The saved samples carry a lesson: our smaller crops today are not natural. They are the result of our sins, as the פסוק in ירמיה says.

keyTerms.meaning: For so we have found, introducing a supporting example
A leading Sage of the Second Temple period
A sample kept for future generations

steps.whyThisMatters: The lesson is not only about rain. The Sages teach that what we lack today is a loss caused by sin, not simply the way nature works.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁכֵּן מָצִינוּ בִּימֵי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן שָׁטַח
phrases.english: For so we found in the days of Shimon ben Shetach
that rain fell for them
on Tuesday nights and on Friday nights,
until wheat grew as big as kidneys,
and barley as big as olive pits,
and lentils as big as gold dinars,
and they tied up some of them as a sample for future generations,
to show how much damage sin causes,
as it is stated: 'Your iniquities have turned away these things,
and your sins have withheld the good from you.'

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁכֵּן מָצִינוּ בִּימֵי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן שָׁטַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a historical example that supports the meaning of בעתם
steps.raayaObject: That 'rain in its season' means rain on Tuesday and Friday nights, and that it brings great blessing
steps.raayaSupportSource: The historical record from the days of שמעון בן שטח, together with the פסוק in ירמיה

steps.title: Rain only at night while the Temple was being built
steps.stepSummary: In the days of הורדוס, while the בית המקדש was being built, rain fell only at night. By morning the skies were clear, so the work could go on. The people understood that Heaven was helping their work.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so we also found in the days of הורדוס. They were busy building the בית המקדש, and rain would fall at night. The next day the wind blew, the clouds scattered, and the sun shone. The people went out to their work, and they knew that they were doing the work of Heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings a second historical example of rain coming at the 'right time.' Here the rain fell only when it would not interrupt the building of the בית המקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This example adds a new idea. In the first story, rain at the right time made the crops grow. Here, the right timing protected a holy work from being disturbed. Because the rain kept avoiding their working hours, the people saw it as a clear sign that Heaven approved of their work.

keyTerms.meaning: Herod, the king who rebuilt the Second Temple
The work of Heaven, a holy task

steps.whatToRemember: Both stories teach the same point. When the people are worthy, rain comes exactly when it helps and never when it gets in the way. This is the meaning of בעתם.

phrases.english: And so we also found in the days of Herod,
that they were busy building the Temple,
and rain would fall at night,
the next day the wind blew,
the clouds scattered, and the sun shone,
and the people went out to their work,
and they knew that the work of Heaven was in their hands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, parallel example supporting the same idea
steps.raayaObject: That rain at the right time is a sign of Heaven's favor
steps.raayaSupportSource: The historical story of the building of the בית המקדש in the days of הורדוס

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about חוני המעגל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה, quoting its opening words about the time people sent a message to חוני המעגל.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה taught: There was an incident in which they sent a message to חוני המעגל, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to a new topic by quoting the משנה. This line sets up the next step, where a ברייתא tells the full story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word וכו׳ ('and so on') shows the גמרא is quoting only the first words of the משנה. The full ברייתא that follows will add many details that the משנה leaves out.

keyTerms.meaning: An incident, a story that happened
Choni the circle-maker, a Sage known for his prayers for rain
And so on, showing the quote continues

phrases.english: The incident in which they sent a message to Choni HaMe'agel, and so on.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new section of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Introduces the משנה's story of חוני המעגל, which will be explained in detail.

steps.title: No rain in אדר, and חוני's first prayer fails
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא tells that most of אדר passed with no rain. The people asked חוני המעגל to pray. He prayed, but no rain fell.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: Once, most of אדר had passed and no rain had fallen. They sent a message to חוני המעגל: 'Pray, and rain will fall!' He prayed, but no rain fell.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that tells the חוני story in detail. It begins with the crisis and with חוני's first prayer, which did not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Having no rain this late in the winter was a serious emergency. The people were sure that חוני's prayers would be answered. His failed first attempt sets up the dramatic step he takes next.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages taught, introducing a ברייתא
Most of the month of אדר
Pray (as a command) or he prayed

steps.confusionAlert: The word הִתְפַּלֵּל appears twice with two meanings. The first time, it is the people's request: 'Pray!' The second time, it describes what חוני did: 'He prayed.'

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: פַּעַם אַחַת יָצָא רוֹב אֲדָר
phrases.english: The Sages taught: Once, most of Adar had passed
and no rain had fallen,
they sent a message to Choni HaMe'agel:
'Pray, and rain will fall!'
He prayed, but no rain fell.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: פַּעַם אַחַת יָצָא רוֹב אֲדָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands on the משנה quoted in Step 4 with a detailed ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The story begins: the drought continues, and חוני's first prayer is not answered.

steps.title: חוני draws a circle like חבקוק
steps.stepSummary: חוני drew a circle and stood inside it, following the example of חבקוק הנביא. A פסוק in חבקוק is the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: He drew a circle and stood inside it, the way the prophet חבקוק did. As it is stated: 'I will stand upon my watch and set myself upon the tower,' and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: After his first prayer fails, חוני takes a dramatic step: he draws a circle and stands in it. The ברייתא shows that this act has a source in what חבקוק did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word מצור can mean a place of confinement. חז"ל read the פסוק to mean that חבקוק shut himself into a kind of enclosure until he received an answer from ה׳‎. חוני copies this, showing he will not leave the circle until rain comes. This act is how he got the name 'המעגל,' the circle-maker.

keyTerms.meaning: Tower or enclosure; read here as a place of confinement

steps.whyThisMatters: The circle explains חוני's nickname 'המעגל.' It also sets up his famous oath in the next lines, that he will not move from the circle until it rains.

phrases.english: He drew a circle and stood inside it,
in the way that Habakkuk the prophet did,
as it is stated: 'Upon my watch I will stand,
and set myself upon the tower (enclosure),' and so on.

steps.triggerLanguage: עָג עוּגָה וְעָמַד בְּתוֹכָהּ, כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁעָשָׂה חֲבַקּוּק הַנָּבִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story: חוני's response after his prayer fails
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חוני draws a circle and stands inside it, based on what חבקוק did, as learned from the פסוק.

steps.title: חוני swears he will not leave the circle until it rains
steps.stepSummary: Standing in his circle, חוני tells ה׳ that the people turned to him because he is like a member of ה׳'s household. He swears by ה׳'s great name not to move until ה׳ has mercy.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said before Him: Master of the World! Your children have turned their faces to me, because I am like a member of Your household before You. I swear by Your great name that I will not move from here until You have mercy on Your children.
steps.whatsHappening: חוני, standing inside the circle from the last step, now speaks his actual prayer. He makes an oath not to leave until it rains.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חוני gives the reason the people came to him: he is like a בן בית, a close member of ה׳'s household. The circle from step 6 now becomes the place where his oath applies. 'I will not move from here' means 'I will not step out of this circle.' This oath drives the whole rest of the story.

keyTerms.meaning: Master of the World, a way of calling out to ה׳
like a member of the household, someone who is close and familiar
I swear, I take an oath

steps.whyThisMatters: The oath explains why the students later say the trickle came only 'to release your oath.' It also sets up the bold, close relationship with ה׳ that חוני shows through the whole story.

phrases.english: He said before Him:
Master of the World!
Your children have turned their faces to me,
because I am like a member of the household before You.
I swear by Your great Name
that I will not move from here
phrases.notes: From here means from inside the circle he drew.

phrases.english: until You have mercy on Your children.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story: after drawing the circle (step 6), חוני now makes his oath-prayer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חוני swears not to leave the circle until ה׳ sends rain.

steps.title: Only a trickle comes, and the students complain
steps.stepSummary: Rain begins to drip lightly. The students say it looks like this rain is only coming to release חוני from his oath, not to save them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rain began to drip. His students said to him: רבי! We look to you so that we will not die. It seems to us that the rain is falling only to release your oath.
steps.whatsHappening: ה׳ answers with just a few drops. The students point out that this is not real help.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A trickle is technically 'rain,' so it might count as fulfilling the oath, but it does nothing for the people. The students are saying they rely on him to save them. These drops only let him leave the circle without breaking his oath.

keyTerms.meaning: dripping, coming down in small drops
we look to you so that we will not die
to release your oath, so you do not break it

phrases.english: Rain began to drip.
His students said to him:
Rabbi! We look to you so that we will not die,
it seems to us that the rain is not falling
except to release your oath.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the first answer to the oath in step 7, and the students' objection to it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A trickle came, and the students say it only serves to release the oath.

steps.title: חוני asks for real rain, and a frightening flood comes
steps.stepSummary: חוני says he asked for rain that fills pits, ditches, and caves. Then furious rain falls, with each drop as big as the mouth of a barrel, at least a לוג.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: This is not what I asked for. I asked for rain that fills pits, ditches, and caves. The rain came down in fury, until every single drop was like the full mouth of a barrel. The Sages estimated that no drop was smaller than a log.
steps.whatsHappening: חוני corrects his request and asks for rain strong enough to fill water storage. The answer swings too far the other way, into a violent storm.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pits, ditches, and caves were where people stored water for the dry season. So חוני is asking for enough rain to last. The storm that comes is huge, and the חכמים measured each drop at a לוג or more. Now there is too much rain.

keyTerms.meaning: this is not what I asked for
pits, ditches, and caves, places for storing water
a measure of liquid, about the volume of six eggs

phrases.english: He said: This is not what I asked for,
rather, rain for pits, ditches, and caves.
It came down with fury,
until every single drop
was like the full mouth of a barrel.
And the Sages estimated
that no drop was less than a log.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר: לֹא כָּךְ שָׁאַלְתִּי, אֶלָּא גִּשְׁמֵי בּוֹרוֹת שִׁיחִין וּמְעָרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: חוני responds to the weak trickle by asking for stronger rain, and gets too much.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חוני asks for storage-filling rain, and a destructive flood falls.

steps.title: The students complain that this rain will destroy the world
steps.stepSummary: Using the same words as before, the students now say this rain seems to be coming to destroy the world.
steps.simpleTranslation: His students said to him: רבי, we look to you so that we will not die. It seems to us that the rain is falling only to destroy the world.
steps.whatsHappening: The students complain a second time, now about the opposite problem: the rain is dangerous.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא repeats the students' exact opening words on purpose. Only the ending changes, from 'to release your oath' to 'to destroy the world.' This shows the swing from too little to too much.

phrases.english: His students said to him:
Rabbi, we look to you so that we will not die,
it seems to us that the rain is not falling
except to destroy the world.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ תַּלְמִידָיו: רַבִּי, רְאִינוּךְ וְלֹא נָמוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same pattern as step 8, but now objects to too much rain instead of too little.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The students say the flood is only coming to destroy the world.

steps.title: חוני asks for blessed rain, and it falls properly
steps.stepSummary: חוני asks for rain of goodwill, blessing, and generosity. It falls in the normal way, but it keeps falling until all the people climb up to הר הבית because of the rain.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said before Him: This is not what I asked for. I asked for rain of goodwill, blessing, and generosity. It fell in its proper way, until all the people went up to the Temple Mount because of the rain.
steps.whatsHappening: חוני corrects his request a third time, and now the rain comes down the right way. But it keeps going so long that the people run to higher ground.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time the quality of the rain is right. The problem is now the amount over time: it does not stop. The people go up to הר הבית because it is high ground, safe from the flooding in ירושלים. This sets up their next request.

keyTerms.meaning: rain of goodwill, blessing, and generosity

phrases.english: He said before Him: This is not what I asked for,
rather, rain of goodwill, blessing, and generosity.
It fell in its proper way,

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁעָלוּ כׇּל הָעָם לְהַר הַבַּיִת,
phrases.english: until all the people went up to the Temple Mount,
because of the rain.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְפָנָיו: לֹא כָּךְ שָׁאַלְתִּי, אֶלָּא גִּשְׁמֵי רָצוֹן בְּרָכָה וּנְדָבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The third and final correction: the rain is now right in kind, but too long in amount.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blessed rain falls properly, but so much that the people go up to הר הבית.

steps.title: The people ask חוני to pray for the rain to stop
steps.stepSummary: The people say: just as you prayed for the rain to come, pray now for it to go away.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: רבי, just as you prayed that it should fall, so pray that it should go away.
steps.whatsHappening: The people make a request that sounds simple and fair. It sets up חוני's surprising answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their reasoning is that if prayer can bring rain, prayer can also stop it. This assumes both prayers are the same kind of request. The next step will show they are not.

phrases.english: They said to him: Rabbi,
just as you prayed that it should fall,
so pray that it should go away.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: רַבִּי, כְּשֵׁם שֶׁהִתְפַּלַּלְתָּ שֶׁיֵּרְדוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reacts to the nonstop rain of step 11 with a request.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Will חוני pray for the rain to stop, the same way he prayed for it to fall?

steps.title: חוני's tradition: we do not pray about too much good
steps.stepSummary: חוני answers that he has a tradition that one does not pray about רוב הטובה, an excess of good.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: This is what I have received as a tradition, that one does not pray about too much good.
steps.whatsHappening: חוני turns down the plain request by quoting a tradition he received from his teachers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Praying for rain to come is asking to be saved from trouble. Praying for rain to stop is asking ה׳ to take away something good, and that is not done. So the 'just as' comparison from step 12 does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: I have received as a tradition

steps.confusionAlert: חוני is not saying the rain is causing no harm. The people really are in trouble. He is saying that, as a rule, one does not ask ה׳ to remove good. Watch how he works around this rule in the next step.
steps.whyThisMatters: This tradition is a source for the idea that one should not pray to remove an overflow of blessing. That is why the next step uses a creative approach.

phrases.english: He said to them: This is what I have received as a tradition,
that one does not pray about too much good.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the request of step 12 by refusing it, based on a tradition.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: One does not pray for an excess of good to be removed.

steps.title: The פר הודאה and חוני's prayer that Israel cannot bear extremes
steps.stepSummary: Even so, חוני asks for a פר הודאה. He leans his hands on it and prays that Israel cannot handle too much good or too much punishment, and asks that the rain stop so there will be relief.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even so, bring me a bull for a thanksgiving offering. They brought him a thanksgiving bull. He leaned both his hands on it and said before Him: Master of the World! Your people Israel, whom You took out of Egypt, cannot handle too much good or too much punishment. When You were angry with them, they could not stand it. When You poured out good on them, they could not stand it. May it be Your will that the rain stop and that there be relief in the world.
steps.whatsHappening: חוני finds a way to help the people without breaking his tradition. He pairs his prayer with a thanksgiving offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By first giving thanks for the good with the פר הודאה, חוני is not rejecting ה׳'s blessing. He phrases the request as a statement about Israel's limits: they cannot bear any extreme. That way, asking for the rain to stop is a request for relief, not a request to remove good.

keyTerms.meaning: a bull brought as a thanksgiving offering
leaned his hands on the animal, as done with offerings (סמיכה)

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי כֵן, הָבִיאוּ לִי פַּר הוֹדָאָה.
phrases.english: Even so, bring me a thanksgiving bull.
They brought him a thanksgiving bull,
he leaned both his hands on it,
and said before Him: Master of the World!
Your people Israel, whom You took out of Egypt,
cannot handle too much good
nor too much punishment.
When You were angry with them, they could not stand it,
phrases.notes: This refers to the drought, when the rain was held back.

phrases.aramaic: הִשְׁפַּעְתָּ עֲלֵיהֶם טוֹבָה — אֵינָן יְכוֹלִין לַעֲמוֹד,
phrases.english: when You poured out good on them, they could not stand it,
phrases.notes: This refers to the overflowing rain.

phrases.english: may it be Your will that the rain stop,
and that there be relief in the world.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף עַל פִּי כֵן, הָבִיאוּ לִי פַּר הוֹדָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Works around the tradition in step 13 by joining thanksgiving with a request for relief.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Together with a thanksgiving offering, חוני prays that the rain stop, because Israel cannot bear extremes.

steps.title: The rain stops at once and the people gather mushrooms
steps.stepSummary: Right away the wind blows, the clouds scatter, and the sun shines. The people go out to the fields and gather truffles and mushrooms.
steps.simpleTranslation: Immediately the wind blew, the clouds scattered, and the sun shone. The people went out to the field and brought back truffles and mushrooms for themselves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends this part of the story by showing that חוני's prayer was answered immediately.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The prayer works right away, which shows that the thanksgiving approach was accepted. The truffles and mushrooms that sprang up from the wet ground show that the rain left real blessing behind.
steps.whatToRemember: חוני's rain came in three stages: a trickle, a destructive flood, and then proper blessed rain. He would not pray directly for good to be removed, because of his tradition. Instead he brought a פר הודאה and prayed that Israel cannot bear extremes, and the rain stopped at once.

phrases.english: Immediately the wind blew,
and the clouds scattered,
and the sun shone,
and the people went out to the field
and brought back truffles and mushrooms for themselves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the immediate result of חוני's prayer in step 14.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The prayer joined with thanksgiving worked: the rain stopped, and the blessing it left behind could be enjoyed.

steps.title: שמעון בן שטח says חוני deserves נידוי
steps.stepSummary: שמעון בן שטח sends a message to חוני. He says that if he were anyone else, he would place him in נידוי, because his oath could have caused a חילול השם.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמעון בן שטח sent a message to him: If you were not חוני, I would decree נידוי on you. For if these were years like the years of אליהו, when the keys of rain were in אליהו's hand, wouldn't the name of Heaven be desecrated through you?
steps.whatsHappening: שמעון בן שטח, the leader of the generation, criticizes חוני for the bold way he demanded rain. He says this behavior deserves נידוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier in the story, חוני swore he would not leave his circle until it rained. אליהו once swore that it would NOT rain. If the two oaths ever clashed, one of these holy men would have broken his word, and Heaven's name would be shamed. So חוני's oath was a real risk.

keyTerms.meaning: The head of the Sages in חוני's time
Excommunication, a ban placed on someone who acted wrongly
The 'keys of rain', meaning control over whether rain falls
Desecration of Heaven's name, a shame to God's honor

steps.confusionAlert: שמעון בן שטח is not saying חוני lied. He is saying the oath was dangerous: if חוני's oath had clashed with אליהו's oath, one of them would have been broken.

phrases.english: Shimon ben Shetach sent to him:
If you were not Choni,
I would decree excommunication upon you.
For if these were years like the years of Eliyahu,
phrases.notes: In אליהו's time there was a drought decreed by his oath.

phrases.english: when the keys of rain were in Eliyahu's hand,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נִמְצָא שֵׁם שָׁמַיִם מִתְחַלֵּל עַל יָדְךָ,
phrases.english: would not the name of Heaven be found desecrated through you?
phrases.notes: A rhetorical question: one of the two oaths would have been broken.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the rain story ends, the גמרא brings a critical reaction to חוני's behavior.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חוני's oath-like demand of Heaven deserved נידוי, because it risked a חילול השם.

steps.title: שמעון בן שטח cannot punish חוני because God treats him like a beloved son
steps.stepSummary: שמעון בן שטח says he cannot act against חוני. חוני is like a spoiled child whose father gives him whatever he asks, and a verse describes him.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what can I do to you? You nag before God and He does what you want, like a son who nags his father and the father does what he wants. The son says: Father, take me to bathe in hot water; rinse me with cold water; give me nuts, almonds, peaches and pomegranates, and the father gives him. About you the verse says: 'Your father and mother will be glad, and she who bore you will rejoice.'
steps.whatsHappening: שמעון בן שטח takes back his threat. He explains that חוני has a special close relationship with God, so he cannot be punished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The child's requests even contradict each other (hot water, then cold), yet the loving father gives him everything. In the same way, חוני asked for rain, then a different kind of rain, then for it to stop, and God gave him each one. The verse from משלי shows that God takes joy in this closeness, so the criticism turns into a kind of praise.

keyTerms.meaning: Nags or pleads like a pampered child
'She who bore you will rejoice' (משלי כג:כה)

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why חוני's unusual behavior was allowed. It was not a normal way to pray. It worked only because of his unique closeness to God.

phrases.english: But what can I do to you,
for you nag before God
and He does your will for you,
like a son who nags his father
and he does his will for him,
and he says to him: Father,
take me to bathe me in hot water.
Rinse me with cold water.
phrases.notes: The opposite of the last request, like חוני's changing requests.

phrases.aramaic: תֵּן לִי אֱגוֹזִים, שְׁקֵדִים, אֲפַרְסְקִים וְרִמּוֹנִים —
phrases.english: Give me nuts, almonds, peaches and pomegranates —
and he gives him.
And about you the verse says:
"Your father and mother will be glad, and she who bore you will rejoice."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the threat of נידוי from step 16 around: the punishment cannot happen because of חוני's special status.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חוני is like a beloved son whose Father grants his every request, so he cannot be put in נידוי.

steps.title: The סנהדרין sends חוני a verse of praise
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reports that the Sages of לשכת הגזית sent חוני a verse from איוב praising him.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: What did the members of לשכת הגזית send to חוני המעגל? 'You shall decree a matter and it will be fulfilled for you, and light will shine on your ways.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with a second, fully positive reaction to חוני, this time from the great סנהדרין. This line quotes the verse, and the next step explains it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'מה שלחו' look like a question, but they are only an opening that introduces the message. Unlike שמעון בן שטח's mixed reaction, the סנהדרין's message is pure praise.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Rabbis taught', which introduces a ברייתא
The Chamber of Hewn Stone, where the great סנהדרין sat
Choni 'the circle-maker', who drew a circle and prayed for rain

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
What did the members of the Chamber of Hewn Stone send
to Choni the Circle-Maker?
"You shall decree a matter and it will be fulfilled for you,
and on your ways light will shine."

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מָה שָׁלְחוּ בְּנֵי לִשְׁכַּת הַגָּזִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second reaction to חוני, from the סנהדרין, in contrast to שמעון בן שטח's mixed response.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The סנהדרין praised חוני with the verse 'ותגזר אומר ויקם לך'.

steps.title: The Sages explain the verse about חוני
steps.stepSummary: The Sages explain the verse phrase by phrase: חוני decrees below and God fulfills it above, and his prayer brought light to a dark generation.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'You shall decree a matter': you decreed from below, and the Holy One, Blessed be He, fulfills your word from above. 'And light will shine on your ways': a generation that was dark, you lit up with your prayer.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains how each part of the verse fits חוני's story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first phrase matches what happened: חוני's words on earth were carried out by הקדוש ברוך הוא in Heaven. The second phrase turns 'light' into a picture. A generation suffering from drought (and spiritual darkness) was brightened through his prayer.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two views of חוני. שמעון בן שטח says his bold behavior deserved נידוי, but he is God's beloved child. The סנהדרין fully praise him: he decrees below, God fulfills it above, and his prayer lit up a dark generation.

phrases.english: "You shall decree a matter" —
you decreed from below,

phrases.aramaic: וְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מְקַיֵּים מַאֲמָרְךָ מִלְמַעְלָה.
phrases.english: and the Holy One, Blessed be He, fulfills your word from above.
"And on your ways light will shine" —
a generation that was dark
you lit up with your prayer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the verse quoted in step 18, phrase by phrase.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חוני's decrees on earth are fulfilled in Heaven, and his prayer brought light to a dark generation.

steps.title: The Sages finish explaining the verse in praise of חוני
steps.stepSummary: The Sages of לשכת הגזית read the last four phrases of the verse from איוב. Each one shows that חוני's תפילה saved a low, sinful, undeserving generation.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'When they are cast down, you will say: lift up.' This means a generation that was low, you raised up with your prayer. 'He saves the one with lowered eyes.' This means a generation bowed down by its sin, you saved with your prayer. 'He rescues the one who is not innocent.' This means a generation that was not innocent, you rescued with your prayer. 'He is rescued by the cleanness of your hands.' This means you rescued it through the clean work of your hands.
steps.whatsHappening: The Sages keep going through the verse one phrase at a time. Each phrase becomes another compliment to חוני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every phrase follows the same pattern: the generation did not deserve rescue, yet חוני's תפילה saved it. The last phrase adds something new. The rescue came through חוני's own clean, honest deeds (מעשה ידיך הברורין), not only through his words.
steps.whatToRemember: The Sages' final verdict is that חוני saved a generation that did not deserve saving, through both his תפילה and his pure deeds.

phrases.english: 'When they are cast down, you will say: lift up'
A generation that was low
you raised it up with your prayer.
'And He saves the one with lowered eyes'
A generation that was bowed down by its sin
you saved it with your prayer.
'He rescues the one who is not innocent'
A generation that was not innocent
you rescued it with your prayer.
'And he is rescued by the cleanness of your hands'
you rescued it through the clean work of your hands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the phrase-by-phrase reading of the verse that began in step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חוני's prayer and pure deeds rescued an undeserving generation.

steps.title: חוני is troubled by the verse 'we were like dreamers'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says חוני struggled his whole life with a verse in תהלים. It compares the seventy-year exile to a dream, and he asked how anyone could sleep seventy years.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: All the days of that righteous man, he was troubled by this verse: 'A song of ascents: When God brought back the returnees to Zion, we were like dreamers.' He said: Is there anyone who sleeps seventy years in a dream?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a brand-new story about חוני. This line sets up the puzzle that the rest of the story will answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse calls the seventy years of גלות בבל a 'dream.' חוני could not see how that comparison works, because no one dreams for seventy years. The story that follows answers his question through his own life.

keyTerms.meaning: The return to Zion from the Babylonian exile

steps.confusionAlert: This is a new story. It is not part of the rain story about חוני that came before. Watch how the seventy years ties back to his question.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
All the days of that righteous man,
he was troubled by this verse:
'A song of ascents:
When God brought back the returnees to Zion,
we were like dreamers,'
He said: Is there anyone
who sleeps seventy years in a dream?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: כׇּל יָמָיו שֶׁל אוֹתוֹ צַדִּיק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new story about חוני, separate from the rain story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חוני could not understand how a seventy-year exile could be called a dream.

steps.title: חוני meets a man planting a carob tree
steps.stepSummary: On the road, חוני sees a man planting a carob tree. He asks how long it takes to bear fruit, and the man answers seventy years.
steps.simpleTranslation: One day he was walking on the road. He saw a certain man planting a carob tree. He said to him: This tree, after how many years does it bear fruit? He said to him: After seventy years.
steps.whatsHappening: The story moves forward. חוני's question gets the number 'seventy years' onto the table, which sets up the next scene.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The number seventy is not random. It matches the seventy years in the verse that troubled חוני, so the story is already pointing toward his answer.

phrases.english: One day he was walking on the road,
he saw a certain man
who was planting a carob tree.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הַאי, עַד כַּמָּה שְׁנִין טָעֵין?
phrases.english: He said to him: This one, after how many years does it bear fruit?
He said to him: After seventy years.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story that grows out of חוני's puzzle.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A carob tree takes seventy years to bear fruit.

steps.title: The planter explains he plants for his grandchildren
steps.stepSummary: חוני asks whether the man is sure he will live seventy years. The man answers that he found carob trees planted by his ancestors, and now he plants for his own descendants.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Is it obvious to you that you will live seventy years? He said to him: I found the world with carob trees. Just as my ancestors planted for me, I too am planting for my children.
steps.whatsHappening: חוני challenges the man's planting, and the man explains why he plants anyway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חוני assumes you plant only for your own benefit. The man answers that he himself eats from trees he never planted, so he plants for the next generations. This sets up the moment when חוני will see the fruit of this very tree.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the famous source for the idea that a person should build for future generations, even when he will not see the results himself.

phrases.english: He said to him: Is it obvious to you
that you will live seventy years?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֲנָא חָרוּבָא בְּעָלְמָא אַשְׁכְּחֵיהּ.
phrases.english: He said to him: I found the world with carob trees.
Just as my ancestors planted for me,
I too am planting for my children.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: פְּשִׁיטָא לָךְ דְּחָיֵית שִׁבְעִין שְׁנִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the planter's reasoning in light of the seventy years just mentioned.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One plants for future generations, just as earlier generations planted for us.

steps.title: חוני falls asleep for seventy years
steps.stepSummary: חוני sits down to eat, falls asleep, and a rock formation hides him from view. He sleeps for seventy years.
steps.simpleTranslation: He sat and ate bread. Sleep came over him, and he slept. A rock formation closed around him, he was hidden from sight, and he slept seventy years.
steps.whatsHappening: The story's turning point: חוני himself now sleeps for seventy years.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חוני asked whether anyone could sleep seventy years, and now it happens to him. The rock hides him, which explains how nobody found or disturbed him all that time.

phrases.english: He sat and ate bread,
sleep came over him, and he slept.
A rock formation closed around him,
he was hidden from sight,
and he slept seventy years.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The story moves forward: חוני's puzzle now comes true in his own life.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חוני slept hidden for seventy years.

steps.title: חוני wakes up and realizes seventy years have passed
steps.stepSummary: חוני wakes and sees a man picking carobs. The man is the grandson of the planter. חוני concludes he slept seventy years, and he sees his donkey has produced many generations.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he got up, he saw a certain man picking carobs from the tree. He said to him: Are you the one who planted it? He said to him: I am his son's son. He said: I can learn from this that I slept seventy years. He saw that his donkey had produced herds upon herds of offspring.
steps.whatsHappening: חוני wakes up and figures out how long he slept. Two clues show it: the grandson picking the carobs, and his donkey's many descendants.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The carob tree the man planted is now bearing fruit for the planter's grandson, exactly as the planter said it would. That proves seventy years have passed. The donkey's herds confirm it. The next step continues the story when חוני goes home.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this, so it follows

phrases.english: When he got up, he saw a certain man
who was picking from them (the carobs).
He said to him: Are you the one who planted it?
He said to him: I am his son's son.
He said: Learn from this
that I slept seventy years.
He saw his donkey
which had produced herds upon herds of offspring.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows what חוני found when he woke from the sleep in step 24.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From the grandson and the donkey's herds, חוני realized he had slept seventy years.

steps.title: חוני returns home and his family does not believe him
steps.stepSummary: חוני goes home and asks whether his son is alive. He is told the son has died but a grandson is alive. When he says he is חוני המעגל, no one believes him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He went to his house and said to them: Is the son of חוני המעגל alive? They said to him: His son is no longer here, but his son's son is. He said to them: I am חוני המעגל. They did not believe him.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues. חוני comes home after his seventy-year sleep, and his own family does not believe who he is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His question about his son shows he is still trying to find the world he knew. The answer confirms that two generations have passed. He has become a stranger in his own home.

phrases.english: He went to his house and said to them:
Is the son of Choni HaMe'aggel alive?
They said to him: His son is no longer here,
but his son's son is here.
phrases.notes: This confirms two generations have passed, matching what he saw with the carob tree.

phrases.english: He said to them: I am Choni HaMe'aggel.
They did not believe him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story right after חוני realizes he slept seventy years.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חוני's family does not recognize or believe him after seventy years.

steps.title: In the בית המדרש, the רבנן praise חוני but do not believe him
steps.stepSummary: In the בית המדרש, חוני hears the רבנן praising him: in his days, he answered every question they had. He tells them he is חוני, but they do not believe him and do not honor him properly.
steps.simpleTranslation: He went to the study hall. He heard the scholars saying: 'Our teachings are as clear as they were in the years of חוני המעגל. When he came into the study hall, he would answer every difficult question the scholars had.' He said to them: 'I am he.' But they did not believe him, and they did not give him the honor he deserved.
steps.whatsHappening: חוני tries again, this time in the בית המדרש. The scholars there speak of him with great respect, yet they still refuse to believe it is really him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a painful twist here. They praise the memory of חוני, but they reject the living חוני standing in front of them. Losing his family's recognition hurt, and now he also loses his place in Torah learning.

phrases.english: He went to the study hall,
and heard the scholars saying:
Our teachings are as clear as in the years of Choni HaMe'aggel,
for when he would enter the study hall,
every difficulty the scholars had,
he would resolve for them.
He said to them: I am he,
but they did not believe him,

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא עָבְדִי לֵיהּ יְקָרָא כִּדְמִבְּעֵי לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: and they did not give him the honor he deserved.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second rejection, this time in the place of Torah learning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even the scholars who praise חוני do not believe or honor him.

steps.title: חוני is heartbroken, prays, and dies
steps.stepSummary: חוני becomes deeply upset, asks for mercy, and dies.
steps.simpleTranslation: He became very upset. He prayed for mercy, and he died.
steps.whatsHappening: The story of חוני ends. Having lost all recognition and companionship, he prays to leave the world, and his prayer is answered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same חוני who once prayed for rain and was answered now prays to die and is answered again. His life without people who know and respect him felt unbearable.

keyTerms.meaning: he became upset or heartbroken (literally, 'his mind grew weak')

phrases.english: He became very upset,
prayed for mercy, and died.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The result of the two rejections.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חוני dies after praying for mercy because no one recognizes him.

steps.title: רבא's lesson: either companionship or death
steps.stepSummary: רבא says this story explains a folk saying: 'Either friendship or death.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: This is what people mean when they say: 'Either friendship or death.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא closes the חוני story with a life lesson. A person without companions feels as if he has no life at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The formula הַיְינוּ דְּאָמְרִי אִינָשֵׁי links a story to a well-known saying. Here the story becomes proof of how much a person needs human connection.

keyTerms.meaning: this is what people say (a formula connecting a story to a popular saying)

steps.whatToRemember: חוני's story ends with רבא's lesson, או חברותא או מיתותא: life without companions and respect is not truly life.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a הלכה about the word חברותא as a study partner only. It refers to human companionship and community in general.

phrases.english: Rava said:
This is what people say:
Either friendship or death.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the moral from חוני's death.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A person needs companionship. Without it, one is like dead.

steps.title: Introducing אבא חלקיה, חוני's grandson, who prayed for rain
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces אבא חלקיה, חוני's grandson. Whenever rain was needed, the רבנן sent for him, he prayed, and rain came.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבא חלקיה was the grandson of חוני המעגל. Whenever the world needed rain, the scholars would send messengers to him. He would pray for mercy, and rain would come.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new story about חוני's family. This line sets up the background for what happens next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It establishes that the power of prayer for rain continued in חוני's family. It also sets up the specific episode that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: חוני's grandson, known for his prayers for rain

phrases.aramaic: אַבָּא חִלְקִיָּה בַּר בְּרֵיהּ דְּחוֹנִי הַמְעַגֵּל הֲוָה,
phrases.english: Abba Chilkiya was the grandson of Choni HaMe'aggel,
and when the world needed rain,
the scholars would send to him,
and he would pray for mercy, and rain would come.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּא חִלְקִיָּה בַּר בְּרֵיהּ דְּחוֹנִי הַמְעַגֵּל הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from חוני's story to a new story about his grandson.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אבא חלקיה's prayers for rain were regularly answered.

steps.title: Two scholars go looking for אבא חלקיה and find him hoeing in a field
steps.stepSummary: Once, during a drought, the רבנן sent two scholars to ask אבא חלקיה to pray. He was not at home. They found him hoeing in a field and greeted him.
steps.simpleTranslation: One time the world needed rain. The scholars sent a pair of scholars to him to ask him to pray for rain. They went to his house but did not find him. They went to the field and found him hoeing, and they greeted him.
steps.whatsHappening: The specific story begins. The scholars find this great man doing simple farm work and greet him. The story continues on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We learn that this famous צדיק works as an ordinary laborer. The greeting sets up the next scene, where his surprising reaction will become important.

phrases.english: One time the world needed rain,
the scholars sent a pair of scholars to him
so that he would pray for mercy and rain would come.
They went to his house but did not find him,
they went to the field and found him
hoeing the ground,
and they greeted him,
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the general background to one specific episode.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The scholars find אבא חלקיה working as a laborer in a field and greet him.
